title: Castling: the one move where two pieces move at once
description: It looks like cheating the first time you see it: the king jumps two squares and the rook hops over him. Castling is the only move in chess that moves two of your pieces — and the only time the king moves more than one square.

body.heading: Two pieces, one move
paragraphs: In castling, the king moves two squares towards one of his rooks, and that rook jumps over the king to land on the square the king crossed. It is the only move in chess where two of your own pieces move on the same turn, and the only legal way a king ever travels more than one square at a time.

Castle towards the corner your rook starts in and it is called kingside; castle the longer way, towards the other rook, and it is queenside. Either way, one move tucks the king behind a wall of pawns and connects your two rooks — two jobs done for the price of one turn.

body.heading: The four conditions
paragraphs: Castling is a privilege, not a right, and it is lost easily. Neither the king nor the chosen rook may have moved at any earlier point in the game — move the rook once and bring it back, and castling on that side is gone forever.

The squares between king and rook must be empty, the king may not currently be in check, and he may not pass through or land on a square attacked by an enemy piece. He may, however, castle even if the rook itself is under attack.

body.heading: Why strong players castle early
paragraphs: A king left in the centre is a king standing in the road where the fighting will be fiercest, so most games see both players castle within the first ten or so moves. Beginners often delay it because the king feels safe enough — right up until the centre opens and he suddenly is not.
Try this in your next game: count how many moves it takes you to castle, and aim to make it sooner. It is the closest thing chess has to free safety.

takeaway: Castling moves king and rook together, tucks the king away and joins your rooks — but only if neither piece has moved and the king's path is safe.
